prompt: Interior of an ordinary modern Korean apartment living room at about 4 pm in late autumn. A large traditional Korean jogakbo (patchwork wrapping cloth) sewn from translucent ramie (mosi) hangs as a curtain over a tall window. The patches are irregular rectangles of different sizes in faded indigo, persimmon orange, pale jade green, soft pink and undyed beige, and several patches are clearly cut from everyday old clothes: a faded blue gingham shirt, a small baby onesie printed with tiny stars, a worn piece of denim with a seam. The hand-stitched seams (fine double stitching) glow as thin bright lines where the light passes. Sunlight through the cloth projects a soft, slightly blurred colored patchwork of light across a pale oak floor. A small child of about five, seen only from behind with no face visible, sits cross-legged inside the colored light looking up at the cloth. Beside a flat floor cushion sits a low wooden sewing box with a few thread spools and a pincushion. Vertical composition: the cloth fills the upper two thirds, the projected light and child the lower third. Eye-level camera, 50mm lens, deep but natural depth of field.
style: Fine-art medium-format film photograph, Kodak Portra 400 look, natural late-afternoon window light, soft fine film grain, true-to-life muted colors, gentle highlight roll-off, slightly imperfect real-world textures (dust in the air, worn wood, loose threads). No HDR, no glossy CGI look, no oversaturation, no symmetry for its own sake, no text, no letters, no watermark, no logo.
